title: Eureka Brass Band around 1944-45
summary: He played B-flat clarinet with Eureka for about a year, ignoring E-flat parts.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Do you remember the band you were playing when you first started to make different variations and put different things in?

No, I don't. We didn't talk about the Eureka Heart at all. No. You were with them, I know, around 44 or 45, because you were in that book of jazz ways. Yeah. Yeah, I was with them a while. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I imagine about a year.
What kind of clarinet did you play in that band? The B-flat. B-flat. You never had any B-flat parts, huh?

I mean, you couldn't, for a, in the Eureka and the Margie's, all that's E-flat parts, didn't you? Yeah. How'd you make out? Well, I just, I just go ahead and play my ideas. Well, you didn't use that? I didn't ever. You see, I could use a tenor saxophone part of all. Oh, you play tenor? No, saxophone parts. Oh, I see. Tenor saxophone parts. Oh, I see. So you got around at that one. Yeah. You must have played with some other brass bands. I think you mentioned the John McConnier. Oh, yeah. Well, that was only on the carnival. That was only on the carnival den. Was the den that band ever? I'm trying to remember. Yeah. Yeah.
